speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome, mother. I can see your newborn has a generalized rash; could you tell me when you first noticed the skin changes, and has the baby had any fever or been feeding well? To help narrow this down, I will need to see the rash clearly.

REQUEST IMAGES: Skin_rash_newborn

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; the timing and lack of prenatal care raise concerns for an infectious etiology like gonococcal sepsis. Have you noticed the baby looking lethargic, refusing feeds, or having a fever, and is there any pus or crusting visible on the rash?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of pustules on an erythematous base with sparing of the palms and soles in a 4-day-old infant is highly suggestive of disseminated gonococcal infection. To confirm this, I need to see the specific lesions and obtain a sample for culture. REQUEST IMAGES: Skin_rash_close_up; REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture_and_Gonococcal_PCR. Have the baby had any eye drainage or been irritable?
